actions.label: Provide food or compensation to guards and their families
Distribute food equally to all refugee groups without diverting it to guards
Permit escorted FWB nutritional assessment in the camp
Organize food distribution through existing guard structures
Grant FWB staff coordinated, escorted access to the camp for food distribution
Involve local partners such as MASHA in distribution
Distribute rations equally to all refugee groups without exclusions
Complete and support FWB documentation for donor accountability
Carry out distribution through existing guard structures

goals.label: Ongoing, sustained food aid supply to the camp
Refugees receive adequate food and nutrition
Burdensome assessments and procedures imposed on the camp
Commander's authority and standing with guards and militia leader
Commander's control of narrative and relationships with local aid partners
Commander's personal safety and legal exposure
FWB controls and oversees food distribution
FWB staff have access and freedom of movement in the camp
FWB's neutrality and impartiality preserved
FWB's reputation and donor funding
Food aid is diverted to guards, militia or their families
Food is distributed fairly and equally to all refugee groups
Guards and their families are fed and compensated
Host town stability and local economy
Militia and guards control food distribution and camp operations
Refugees stay contained and do not reach the capital
Safety of FWB staff and local assistants
Suspected terrorists or hostile actors benefit from aid or access
Aid is documented and accountable to meet donor requirements
Reliable data on refugees' nutritional needs

redLines.label: Allow FWB representatives and FWB-chosen assistants to manage ration handover
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Hire local assistants and partner with known local actors such as MASHA
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Manage food disbursement directly through FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Provide food or compensation to guards and their families
redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head. Or someone in your family's head.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
